description: WM-605 retrieval-quality corpus. Hand-written, modeled on coding-agent project memory (not taken from any user store). Each query is a paraphrase of what an agent would ask; `target` is the one applicable memory. Hard negatives: superseded predecessors, contradicted facts, and another session's private notes must never be returned in place of the target.

memories.text: Install dependencies with pnpm; npm and yarn lockfiles are rejected by CI.
The build requires Node 22 or newer because it uses the built-in sqlite module.
Database migrations live in db/migrations and run in filename order at startup.
Name migration files with a UTC timestamp prefix like 20260101_1200_add_users.sql.
Never commit .env files; secrets are loaded from the vault at deploy time.
Feature flags default to off for enterprise tenants and are toggled in the admin console.
The public API is rate limited to 600 requests per minute per token.
Outbound webhook delivery retries five times with exponential backoff starting at two seconds.
Use the structured logger from src/log.ts; console.log is blocked by the linter.
Store every timestamp in UTC and convert to the user's zone only in the UI layer.
Integration tests use a throwaway Postgres container started by the test harness, never the shared staging database.
Update UI snapshots with pnpm test -u only after reviewing the diff by hand.
Branch names follow type/short-description, for example fix/login-redirect.
Pull requests are squash-merged; the PR title becomes the commit message.
Releases are cut from main by tagging vX.Y.Z; the release workflow builds and signs artifacts.
The product catalog cache expires after 15 minutes and is invalidated on price changes.
Thumbnails are generated at 128, 256 and 512 pixels; animated images are skipped.
Access tokens live 15 minutes; refresh tokens live 30 days and rotate on every use.
CORS allows only the app and admin origins; wildcard origins are forbidden.
List endpoints use cursor pagination; offset pagination was removed for performance.
Shared types live in packages/types and must not import from application packages.
User-facing strings go through the t() helper; hard-coded English text fails review.
API errors return a stable machine-readable code field alongside the human message.
Production database backups run nightly at 02:00 UTC and are kept for 35 days.
Pages for the payments service go to the payments on-call rotation, not the platform team.
Deprecated endpoints keep working for two minor releases and log a warning header.
CSV exports stream rows instead of buffering so large reports do not exhaust memory.
Reindex the search cluster after changing analyzers; partial reindexing corrupts relevance.
Uploads larger than 100 MB must use the multipart endpoint.
Every interactive element needs a visible focus style and an accessible name.
Dark mode colors are derived from design tokens; never hard-code hex values in components.
Background jobs run on the queue worker; HTTP handlers must not do work longer than 200 ms.
Expose service metrics on /metrics in Prometheus format; label cardinality must stay bounded.
The checkout end-to-end test is flaky on Windows because of file locking; rerun before investigating.
Golden files under tests/golden are regenerated by scripts/regen-golden.ts, never edited by hand.
New dependencies must use a permissive license; GPL packages need legal approval.
Transactional email templates are MJML files compiled at build time.
Geocoding results are cached per postal code for seven days.
Locale fallback resolves the regional variant first, then the base language, then English.
Payroll exports must be finished before the fifth business day of the month.

negatives.text: Before the gateway migration, each API token could make only 100 calls a minute.
Builds were pinned to Node 18 while the old bundler crashed on newer runtimes.
Scratch note: product catalog cache expiry seems wrong, maybe 5 minutes?
Private debugging: refresh tokens appear to live 7 days on staging.
Database snapshots of production are taken once a week on Sundays.
